summary: Uses the StereoLabs ZED SDK to scan and create mesh geometry or live point clouds from ZED depth data, usually sourced from a ZED TOP. It supports mesh or point-cloud output, preview modes, camera calibration parameters, depth filtering, normals, and color output.

key_concepts: ZED POP is a Windows-only StereoLabs ZED SDK operator for scanning mesh geometry or producing live point clouds from ZED depth data.
A referenced ZED TOP supplies the depth/video pipeline; the POP is not a generic depth converter and should be guarded by device, SDK, and OS availability.
Output Mode separates accumulated mesh capture from live point-cloud output, and Connectivity controls whether points remain unconnected, point primitives, or triangles.
Capture controls include initialize, start, play, done, preview, maximum memory, spatial mapping resolution, and depth range.
Normals, color, filtering, perspective, rerange, mirror, camera view override, FOV/focal-length conversion, optical center, and near/far deletion shape the resulting mesh or cloud.
Depth filtering and near/far clipping can dramatically change density, continuity, and small-component cleanup, so planners should expose these as validation-sensitive controls.
common_gotchas: ZED POP is Windows-only according to the official docs; guard generated networks on macOS/Linux.
Requires a ZED TOP/SDK/device pipeline; it is not a generic depth-to-POP converter.
Depth near/far deletion and filter settings strongly affect mesh continuity and point-cloud density.
